Automation Readiness Assessment.description_en:
The New Directors Program provides an opportunity for new executives to better understand their role as a director within the Government of Canada. The program's aim is to equip new executives with the skills they need to effectively lead in today's work environment. Participants will explore a variety of leadership topics to help them navigate complexities, be resilient and adaptable in times of change, and enhance their key leadership competencies as a new executive.

 

Topics include:

• understanding the director's role in modern government systems and processes, including the new digital standards

• strengthening self-awareness and the skills to build resilience, lead, engage and collaborate

• exploring the director's role in creating a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace

• developing leadership agility and capacity to navigate complexity

 

Notes:

The New Directors Program is cohort-based and comprises nine modules. These modules include learning sessions, independent and group work, a psychometric self-assessment, and participation in a 360-degree feedback process. Throughout the program, participants will also engage in peer coaching sessions and leadership group discussions.

 

Learn more about the New Directors Program.

Cost-Benefit and Tradeoff Analysis in Di.description_en:
Not to be confused with project management, business analysis offers a unique value to project work. This online self-paced course explores the purpose and benefits of business analysis, and activities such as elicitation, traceability and monitoring, solution evaluation, and needs assessment. Participants will examine the business analyst role, identify its responsibilities, and learn best practices for using product roadmaps and validating project requirements.

 

Topics include:

- explaining the responsibilities of a business analyst
- exploring needs assessment, stakeholder engagement, solution evaluation, and business analysis elicitation activities
- identifying business analysis processes for traceability and monitoring

 

Notes:

This course is intended for all public servants, including those with or without project management experience. Materials are aligned with the PMBOK® Guide – Seventh Edition.

Completion of the 26 courses in the CAPM® course series can count towards the eligibility requirements for the Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM®) exam administered for a fee by the Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
The CAPM® exam is not administered by the Canada School of Public Service. Learners wishing to take the exam are responsible for validating their eligibility directly with PMI.
Cost-Benefit and Tradeoff Analysis in Di.description_fr:
L'analyse d’affaires, à ne pas confondre avec la gestion de projet, offre une valeur unique au travail lié au projet. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre permet d'explorer le but et les avantages de l'analyse commerciale et des activités telles que la collecte d'informations, la traçabilité et le suivi, ainsi que l'évaluation des besoins et des solutions. Les participants examineront le rôle et les responsabilités de l'analyste d’affaires et apprendront les pratiques exemplaires de l'utilisation de feuilles de route de produits et de la validation des exigences d'un projet.


Sujets traités :

- expliquer quelles sont les responsabilités d'un analyste d’affaires;
- explorer les activités de collecte d'informations pour l'évaluation des besoins, la mobilisation des parties prenantes, l'évaluation des solutions et l'analyse d’affaires;
- cerner les processus d'analyse d’affaires pour la traçabilité et la surveillance.


Remarques :

Ce cours s'adresse à tous les fonctionnaires, qu'ils aient ou non de l'expérience en gestion de projet. Le matériel est conforme à la septième édition du Guide PMBOK®.

La réussite des 26 cours de série de cours CAPM® peut être prise en compte dans les conditions d’admissibilité à l’examen payant d’Associé certifié en gestion de projet (CAPM®) du Project Management Institute (PMI).
 
L’examen CAPM® n’est pas offert par l’École de la fonction publique du Canada. Les apprenants qui souhaitent le passer sont responsables de vérifier leur admissibilité directement auprès du PMI.

The New Directors Program provides an opportunity for new executives to better understand their role as a director within the Government of Canada. The program's aim is to equip new executives with the skills they need to effectively lead in today's work environment. Evidence-based Argumentation for Excepti.title_en: Evidence-Informed Decision-Making: Weighing Evidence for Policy Decisions (TRN505)
Evidence-based Argumentation for Excepti.description_en:
Policy decisions are most likely to achieve their desired outcomes and instill public trust when they are informed by the best available evidence. This online self-paced course explores the process of defining, gathering and weighing evidence that is relevant to a policy decision. Participants will learn why decision-makers and scientists may have different standards of proof for the same factual claim.


Topics include:

· recognizing biases that can skew the evidence on which a decision is based

· weighing evidence to infer whether a claim is true or false, and determining the level of confidence with which this can be done

· acknowledging evidence gaps and the implications of changes to evidence over time

Data Sharing Agreements and Privacy Law.title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
Data Sharing Agreements and Privacy Law.description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

Automation-first approaches.description_en:
Documenting desired business outcomes is a critical part of the decision-making process. This online self-paced course explains how to frame an opportunity by asking the right questions, identifying and testing assumptions, and creating an effective problem statement. Participants will learn about validating assumptions, identifying the opportunity at-hand and ensuring that the proper resources are dedicated to its analysis.

Topics include:

•	making effective data-driven decisions

•	identifying the steps to take to test and validate assumptions

•	asking questions to narrow down a problem

•	defining an initial problem statement •	refining and finalizing problem statements

Notes:

This course was developed with subject matter support from the International Institute for Analytics.

Automation-first approaches.title_en: Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner, Part 1: Fundamentals (COR118)
Automation-first approaches.description_en:
HR practitioners play a crucial role in allowing an organization to provide strategic guidance and make informed decisions on matters of human resourcing. This online self-paced course examines the strategic role of senior HR practitioners, the different HR perspectives, and the forward-thinking skills needed to provide strategic HR guidance. Participants will learn about the analytics tools available to them and how to conduct in-depth analyses, propose risk-informed solutions, and address complex and strategic HR challenges.

 

Topics include:

·        reviewing the concepts of strategic perspectives and strategic behaviour

·        defining the strategic role of senior HR practitioners

·        identifying the steps in a comprehensive strategic analysis

·        proposing options based on a risk evaluation

·        exploring analytics tools that can assist with strategic HR decisions

 

Notes:

This course is part 1 of a two-part course suite, which begins with the prerequisite Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner: Fundamentals (COR118) (online self-paced), followed by Becoming a Strategic HR Practitioner: From Theory to Practice (COR128) (virtual instructor-led).
